reason: Nergal is the Mesopotamian god of war and plague; the lion of Kutha embodies the raw, sanctioned force that defense and strategic studies still theorize.
By marriage to Ereshkigal, Nergal becomes king of the underworld — a ruler of the dead and the geography of grief.
As plague-bringer and the burning fever personified, Nergal names the ancient terror that public health and epidemiology exist to contain.
The Epic of Erra makes him the agent of war, fire, and epidemic catastrophe — the scenario the resilience sector plans against.
